newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower in a bear hug.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower in a bear hug.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower as bearish sentiment gripped the market, traders said. Volume was light.
"It boils down to this: we had weak outside markets, export business went outside the U.S., and basis bids weakened," a KCBT trader said.
Basis bids for ordinary HRW wheat on railcars through or to Kansas City eased by three cents Monday, KCBT said.
Meanwhile, the market appeared to reflect only slight disappointment at news that Pakistan opted to buy 225,000 tonnes of Australian wheat instead of U.S. wheat.
Wheat drew spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, which slipped on near-ideal soy crop weather in South America.
KCBT wheat settled one to 4-1/2 cents lower, with December down 1-1/2 cents at $4.38 per bushel. March lost 2-1/2 cents to close at $3.93.
Losses in the December contract were limited by the lack of deliveries. Meanwhile, the July contract lost ground amid continued reports of good condition of HRW wheat in the U.S. High Plains.
Traders said Term Commodities, a unit of Dreyfus, bought one million July bushels and CIS bought 1.2 million March.
